setting: A fictional conversation with a colleague about applying a real uploaded company document at work.

presentation.situation: A colleague asks you to apply a rule from your uploaded company document.
presentation.opening: Have you got a minute? I need to know what our policy says about this.

brief.you_are: You are an employee who knows how to use the company's documents.
brief.situation: A colleague wants to know how a company rule applies. The relevant passage from your uploaded document appears in your lesson sources.
brief.task: Say what the document actually requires, apply it to your colleague's situation, and be honest about anything the document does not cover.
brief.done_looks_like: Your colleague knows the rule, what to do now, and who to check with for anything not covered.

participants.name: You
participants.relationship: Colleague asked for help with a company rule

participants.name: Jamie
participants.relationship: A colleague in a hurry who wants a quick answer

card.want: A quick answer about the rule, ideally that a step can be skipped.
card.hidden_need: Is under time pressure from a manager and does not want to get it wrong.
card.attitude: Friendly, rushed, and tempted to cut a corner.
tactics: Ask whether a step can be skipped just this once
Ask 'are you sure that's what it says?'
Ask something the document might not cover

pressure.challenging: Claims that a manager said it was fine.

ledger.text: Jamie has not read the document and depends on what the learner says about it.
Jamie would like to skip a step to save time, but has no authority to approve an exception.

objectives.description: State what the document actually requires
objectives.evidence: The learner accurately refers to what the source passage says, without inventing a rule.
alternatives: The document says this step has to be done first

objectives.description: Apply the rule to the situation
objectives.evidence: The learner says what the colleague should do in this situation, based on the document.
alternatives: So in your case, you still need to do that step before you go ahead

objectives.description: Handle what the document does not cover
objectives.evidence: The learner acknowledges uncertainty and says how to verify it, rather than guessing or inventing.
alternatives: The document doesn't cover that, so I'd check with the policy owner

examples: It doesn't cover that, so I'd check with ...
prerequisites: Upload a readable company document and select it for this lesson.

beats.goal: Find out what the rule actually says.
opportunity: So what does it actually say?
Are you sure that's what it says?
beats.orient: I'm asking you what our company document says. Look at the passage in your lesson sources, and tell me the rule in your own words.
fallback: What does the document actually say?
Can you tell me the rule?

beats.goal: Apply it, and resist a shortcut.
signals: \b(?:so you|you (?:need|should|must|have to)|in your case|i would|don'?t skip|can'?t skip|first you|you can'?t)\b
opportunity: So what should I do right now? Can I skip that part, just this once?
My manager's in a hurry. Does that change anything?
beats.orient: Now tell me what I should do in my situation. I'd like to skip a step. Does the document allow that?
fallback: So what should I do right now?
Can I skip that part, just this once?

beats.goal: Ask about something the document may not cover.
opportunity: And what if this is a special case that isn't in there? What then?
What if it doesn't say anything about my situation?
beats.orient: Last question: what should I do when the document doesn't cover my case? It's fine to say you don't know, and tell me who to ask.
fallback: What if the document doesn't cover my situation?
Who should I ask, if it isn't in there?

closing_line: Great, thanks. I'll do it properly, then.

o1.good: Staying close to what the passage says, in your own words, without adding to it.
common_mistakes: Stating a rule the document does not contain
o1.micro_lesson: Say what the document actually says, not what seems sensible.
o1.model: According to the document, this step has to be done before you go ahead.
o1.smaller_step: Read the passage, then say one thing it requires.

o2.good: Turning the rule into a clear instruction for this person, and holding firm if the rule does not allow the shortcut.
common_mistakes: Quoting the rule with no advice
o2.micro_lesson: Finish the rule with what this person should do now.
o2.model: So in your case, you still need to do that step, even if your manager is in a hurry.
o2.smaller_step: Tell Jamie one thing to do next.

o3.good: Saying clearly where the document stops, and naming how to find out.
o3.micro_lesson: 'It doesn't say' is a good answer, if you add who to check with.
o3.model: The document doesn't cover that, so I'd check with the policy owner before going ahead.
